newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sugar in copper foil deal with Japan firms.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sugar in copper foil deal with Japan firms.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp said on Friday it had signed a T$2.25 billion (US$81.8 million) deal with three Japanese firms to build a copper foil plant.
Taiwan Sugar holds 45 percent of the venture, a company manager, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
The copper foil plant, located in the southern city of Touliu, will be completed by December 1998 and will produce 5,100 tonnes of copper foil annually, she added.

Japan's Furukawa Electric Company, trading company Nichimen Corp, and Furukawa Circuit Foil have the remaining 55 percent in the venture, she said. Furukawa Circuit Foil is a subsidiary of Furukawa Electric.

Taiwan imports more than 10,000 tonnes of copper foil a year, 60 percent of which is from Japan, she said. Copper foil demand is rising in Taiwan as it is a key component in computer and mobile phone manufacturing.
"This copper foil venture will help satisfy the rising demand in Taiwan's high-tech industry," the manager said.
Taiwan Sugar, whose sugar monopoly in Taiwan ends in 2002, has begun branching out into new sectors including real estate, construction and farming. ($1 = T$27.5)
